case_study.title: The Tire Was Already There
case_study.subtitle: Ten Examples of Resonance Inspection, Testing, and Bounded Tuning
case_study.purpose: Demonstrate a reusable structural method for observing system behavior, locating relevant relationships, applying bounded adjustments, and retesting the whole system.
case_study.central_proposition: Inspect the whole. Locate the bit. Tune the relationship. Retest the whole.
case_study.scope_note: The examples range from literal physical resonance to broader systems in which the same inspection grammar is used as a structural analogy. The case study does not claim that mechanical, acoustic, structural, electrical, cybernetic, and informational systems are physically equivalent.

principles.calibration_is_not_creation: The system and its behavior may already exist before calibration begins. Calibration reveals relationships and tests bounded corrections.
principles.resonance_is_contextual: Resonance is neither inherently desirable nor undesirable. The desired response depends on the system and its operating context.
principles.observable_location_is_not_always_causal: The place where behavior becomes visible may differ from the relationship where intervention is appropriate.
principles.local_change_requires_global_retest: An improvement to one component or relationship must be evaluated against the behavior of the whole system.
principles.coherence_is_not_stillness: A coherent system may remain dynamic. Calibration is concerned with improving behavior, not eliminating motion or change.

examples.name: Tire Balancing
examples.inspection: Rotate the wheel and observe its dynamic behavior.
examples.localization: Identify where the rotating assembly's effective mass distribution requires correction.
examples.bounded_tuning: Apply an appropriate balancing correction without redesigning the larger vehicle.
examples.retest: Rotate the wheel again and compare the resulting behavior.
examples.structural_lesson: A small local correction can substantially alter whole-system behavior.
examples.key_phrase: Tune the bit. Retest the whole.

examples.name: Musical Instrument Tuning
examples.stimulus: excitation of a string, membrane, air column, or resonant body
examples.observable_response: pitch, harmonics, beating, and interaction among frequencies
examples.inspection: Excite the instrument and observe its acoustic response.
examples.localization: Identify the parameter responsible for the relevant frequency relationship.
examples.bounded_tuning: Adjust an appropriate parameter such as tension or effective length.
examples.retest: Excite the instrument again and compare the resulting response.
examples.structural_lesson: Resonance is neither inherently good nor inherently bad. Context determines whether alignment, attenuation, or displacement is desirable.

examples.name: Structural Vibration
examples.system: building, bridge, tower, or comparable structure
examples.observable_response: modes, oscillation, or amplified structural response
examples.inspection: Characterize how the structure responds to relevant excitation.
examples.localization: Determine which structural relationship contributes to the undesirable response.
examples.bounded_tuning: Modify an appropriate structural, mass, stiffness, or damping relationship.
examples.retest: Measure the structural response again after the intervention.
examples.structural_lesson: The location where a problem becomes visible is not necessarily the location where the most effective correction belongs.

examples.name: Washing Machine Spin Cycle
examples.relationship_to_resonance: physical vibration across changing operating states
examples.system: washing machine, rotating load, supports, and surrounding mechanical relationships
examples.inspection: Observe system behavior across multiple operating states.
examples.localization: Identify load, support, leveling, damping, or design relationships associated with the unwanted behavior.
examples.bounded_tuning: Correct the relevant relationship where justified.
examples.structural_lesson: A system can appear coherent in one operating state and become unstable in another.

examples.name: Rotating Machinery
examples.system: motor, pump, fan, turbine, gearbox, or other rotating machinery
examples.stimulus: operation across a range of rotational conditions
examples.observable_response: vibration peaks or changing dynamic behavior
examples.inspection: Observe the machine across its operating range.
examples.localization: Distinguish the component displaying the symptom from the relationship producing it.
examples.bounded_tuning: Address the relevant excitation or system relationship.
examples.retest: Repeat the operating range and compare responses.
examples.structural_lesson: Observable location and causal location are different questions.

examples.name: Vehicle Suspension
examples.system: road, tire, wheel, suspension, chassis, seat, and occupant
examples.observable_response: movement, transmitted vibration, oscillation, and settling behavior
examples.inspection: Introduce known or repeatable disturbances and observe the coupled response.
examples.localization: Identify which subsystem relationship contributes to undesirable behavior.
examples.retest: Repeat the disturbance and inspect both local and system-wide consequences.
examples.structural_lesson: Local improvement must be evaluated against system-level behavior.

whole_bit_relation.whole_to_bit: Use system behavior to locate relationships requiring inspection.
whole_bit_relation.bit_to_whole: Evaluate every local intervention by observing its consequences throughout the larger system.

examples.name: Room Acoustics
examples.relationship_to_resonance: literal acoustic resonance with observer-position dependence
examples.system: sound source, room geometry, surfaces, boundaries, and observer position
examples.observable_response: spatial differences in amplitude, decay, peaks, or nulls
examples.inspection: Excite the environment and observe the response across frequencies and positions.
examples.localization: Determine which source-environment-observer relationships produce the observed behavior.
examples.bounded_tuning: Adjust placement, absorption, diffusion, geometry, or listening position where appropriate.
examples.retest: Measure or listen again from relevant positions.
examples.structural_lesson: Some observed properties belong to relationships rather than isolated objects.
examples.observer_note: Observation should preserve information about position, conditions, and interaction with the system.

examples.name: Electronic and Signal Systems
examples.system: circuit, filter, or related signal-processing system
examples.observable_response: changes in frequency or signal response
examples.inspection: Sweep or vary the input and measure the response.
examples.localization: Identify the component or parameter relationship responsible for the observed response.
examples.bounded_tuning: Modify justified circuit or system parameters.
examples.structural_lesson: Calibration can alter what a system amplifies, attenuates, passes, or rejects without replacing the entire system.

examples.name: Feedback and Control Systems
examples.relationship_to_resonance: structural analogy with possible literal oscillatory behavior
examples.stimulus: input, disturbance, or deviation from a desired condition
examples.observable_response: output behavior including possible overshoot, oscillation, or instability
examples.inspection: Observe output and compare behavior with the desired condition.
examples.localization: Identify which feedback relationship contributes to undesirable behavior.
examples.retest: Return the result of the adjustment through the observation loop.
examples.structural_lesson: A correction becomes meaningful only after its effect re-enters observation.
examples.boundary_note: The resonance-calibration pattern is used here as a structural analogy. The example does not assert that every feedback process is an instance of physical resonance.

examples.name: Human and Machine Knowledge Systems
examples.system: documentation, terminology, diagrams, references, educational material, software, metadata, historical records, and machine-readable structures
examples.stimulus: human or machine traversal, questioning, lookup, interpretation, or validation
examples.observable_response: confusion, missing definitions, contradictions, broken navigation, terminology drift, provenance gaps, or successful traversal
examples.inspection: Probe the knowledge system through questions, references, navigation, machine traversal, and newcomer experience.
examples.localization: Identify the relationship where information becomes unclear, disconnected, contradictory, inaccessible, or difficult to reuse.
bounded_tuning: separate concepts that have drifted together
reconnect concepts that have drifted apart
examples.retest: Traverse the knowledge system again with humans and machines and compare results.
examples.structural_lesson: The knowledge may already exist while its relationships remain poorly calibrated.
examples.key_phrase: The tire was already there. So was the knowledge.

reusable_inspection_grammar.action: Identify amplification, attenuation, drift, oscillation, or instability.
Locate the relationship associated with the behavior.
Repeat the original or equivalent test.
Inspect consequences elsewhere in the system.
Preserve what was learned, including observations, interventions, and results.

whole_to_bits.question: What behavior is visible at the system level, and which relationships deserve closer inspection?
whole_to_bits.purpose: Use whole-system behavior to guide localization.

bits_to_whole.question: After changing a local relationship, what happened to the complete system?
bits_to_whole.purpose: Prevent local optimization from being mistaken for global improvement.

rtt_calibration_view.objective: Observe relationships across time, identify where behavior departs from the intended or coherent regime, make the smallest defensible intervention, and observe again.
not_the_objective: Assume that all cross-domain examples share identical physical mechanisms.
rtt_calibration_view.discipline: Calibration begins with observation rather than assumption.

boundary_conditions.physical_claim: Examples involving mechanical, acoustic, structural, and electrical systems may involve literal physical resonance or frequency response.
boundary_conditions.analogy_claim: Cybernetic and informational examples primarily demonstrate transfer of the inspection and calibration grammar.
boundary_conditions.non_equivalence: Cross-domain structural similarity does not establish physical equivalence.
boundary_conditions.evidence_rule: Observed improvement should be evaluated through retesting rather than inferred from the intention or elegance of an intervention.

closing_principles: Tune the bit. Retest the whole.
Inspect the whole. Locate the bit. Tune the relationship. Retest the whole.
A successful intervention is demonstrated by what the system does afterward.
The goal is not to eliminate dynamics, but to understand them well enough that the system can move without unnecessary internal opposition.
case_study.closing_statement: The tire was already there. We simply learned how to listen to what its motion was telling us.
